## Setup

```{r}
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(sf)
library(tidycensus)
library(purrr)
library(lubridate)
library(stringr)
library(janitor)
library(gt)
```


## 1. ACS Demographic & Economic Data (2019–2024)

Pulls county-level ACS 5-year estimates for New York State across five vintages.
Variables cover population, economic wellbeing, housing, education, and family
structure. Years are pulled individually via `map_dfr()` since `get_acs()` only
accepts one year per call.

```{r}
years <- c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

my_vars <- c(
  # Population & demographics
  tot_pop       = "B01003_001",
  median_age    = "B01002_001",
  white         = "C02003_003",
  black         = "C02003_004",
  asian         = "C02003_006",
  hispanic      = "B03001_003",

  # Economic wellbeing
  medhhinc      = "B25119_001",
  pop_poverty   = "B17001_002",
  pop_poverty_universe = "B17001_001",
  labor_force   = "B23025_003",
  unemployed    = "B23025_005",

  # Housing
  hu_ownocc     = "B25003_002",
  tot_hu        = "B25001_001",
  rent_burden_30_35   = "B25070_007",  # 30.0-34.9%
  rent_burden_35_40   = "B25070_008",  # 35.0-39.9%
  rent_burden_40_50   = "B25070_009",  # 40.0-49.9%
  rent_burden_50plus  = "B25070_010",  # 50.0%+
  rent_total          = "B25070_001",

  # Education
  edu_hs_or_less     = "B15003_017",
  edu_bachelors_plus = "B15003_022",
  edu_total          = "B15003_001",

  # Family structure
  divorced_m    = "B12001_010",
  divorced_f    = "B12001_019",
  single_dad_children = "B11003_010",   # male householder, no wife, with own children <18
  single_mom_children = "B11003_016"    # female householder, no husband, with own children <18
)

census_data_nys <- map_dfr(
  years,
  ~ get_acs(
      geography = "county",
      variables = my_vars,
      state = "NY",
      year = .x,
      survey = "acs5",
      geometry = FALSE,
      cache_table = TRUE
    ) %>%
    mutate(year = .x)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
  arrange(NAME, year)

census_data_nys <- census_data_nys %>%
  mutate(divorced = divorced_m + divorced_f)
```

---

## 2. Prison Facility Data (ICPSR Prison Boundaries)

The raw dataset contains 6,468 prison facilities nationwide with geographic
boundaries. Three filters are applied: (1) only facilities with STATUS "OPEN"
or "CLOSED" are retained, dropping ambiguous statuses; (2) TYPE "COUNTY" is
excluded, removing local jails, which were not sited as economic development
tools and do not fit the study's theoretical framework; (3) restricted to New
York State. The cleaned data is collapsed to the county level via `COUNTYFIPS`,
producing facility counts and capacity/population totals broken out by status.

```{r}
prisons_icpsr <- st_read("data/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson")

prisons_clean_nys <- prisons_icpsr %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(
    STATUS %in% c("OPEN", "CLOSED"),
    TYPE != "COUNTY",
    STATE == "NY"
  )

prisons_by_county_nys <- prisons_clean_nys %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS) %>%
  summarise(
    num_prisons        = n(),
    num_open           = sum(STATUS == "OPEN"),
    num_closed         = sum(STATUS == "CLOSED"),
    capacity_total     = sum(CAPACITY, na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_open      = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_closed    = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_total          = sum(POPULATION, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_open           = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_closed         = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

A lookup of individual NY facility names (used later for matching DOCCS-sourced
files, which use short operational names rather than full official names) is
built here for reuse across several downstream sections.

```{r}
prisons_clean_match_names <- prisons_clean_nys %>%
  mutate(name_clean = trimws(toupper(NAME)))

ny_facility_lookup_full <- prisons_clean_match_names %>%
  select(name_clean, COUNTYFIPS, COUNTY)
```

---

## 3. Community Mortality Rates (CDC — Overdose, Suicide, Homicide)

County-level death rates for drug overdose, homicide, and suicide, restricted
to New York and the years 2019–2024. CDC suppresses small cell counts (1–9
deaths) using a `-999` sentinel value rather than a true missing flag; these
are recoded to `NA` directly here rather than left to corrupt downstream means.

```{r}
injury_overdose_violence <- read_csv("data/injury_overdose_violence.csv")

injury_overdose_violence_nys <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  filter(ST_NAME == "New York") %>%
  filter(Period %in% c("2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024")) %>%
  filter(Intent %in% c("Drug_OD", "All_Suicide", "All_Homicide")) %>%
  mutate(Rate = as.numeric(Rate)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols    = c(GEOID, NAME, ST_GEOID, ST_NAME, Period),
    names_from = Intent,
    values_from = Rate,
    names_glue = "{Intent}_rate"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    overdose_rate = Drug_OD_rate,
    suicide_rate  = All_Suicide_rate,
    homicide_rate = All_Homicide_rate,
    year = Period
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    # CDC suppression sentinel -> true NA (affects small, mostly rural counties)
    suicide_rate  = ifelse(suicide_rate  == -999, NA, suicide_rate),
    homicide_rate = ifelse(homicide_rate == -999, NA, homicide_rate),
    overdose_rate = ifelse(overdose_rate == -999, NA, overdose_rate)
  )
```

## 4. Rural–Urban Classification (USDA RUCC, 2023)

```{r}
rural_2023 <- read_csv("data/rural_urban_codes2023.csv")  # 1-3: urban, 4-9: rural

rural_2023_nys <- rural_2023 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Attribute, values_from = Value) %>%
  mutate(
    Population_2020 = as.numeric(Population_2020),
    RUCC_2023 = as.numeric(RUCC_2023)
  ) %>%
  filter(State == "NY")
```

## 5. Life Expectancy (USALEEP, 2010–2015)

Life expectancy data comes from the USALEEP project, the most comprehensive
source of county-level life expectancy for the contiguous US. The raw file is
at the census tract level, so it is aggregated to the county level using a
population-weighted mean (rather than a simple mean), so more populous tracts
contribute proportionally more to each county estimate. Tract-level population
denominators come from the 2011–2015 ACS 5-year estimates. Tract numbers in the
USALEEP file (e.g. "0201.00") are reformatted into standard 11-digit Census
GEOIDs. The 2010–2015 vintage is the only nationally comprehensive county-level
life expectancy dataset available; the resulting lag relative to the outcome
years (2019–2024) is a noted limitation.

```{r}
life_expectancy <- read_csv("data/life_expectancy_2010-2015.csv")

tract_pop <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c(tract_pop = "B01003_001"),
  state     = "NY",
  year      = 2015,
  survey    = "acs5",
  geometry  = FALSE
) %>%
  select(GEOID, tract_pop = estimate)

fips_xwalk <- fips_codes %>%
  filter(state == "NY") %>%
  mutate(
    county_full = paste0(county, ", ", state),
    county_fips = paste0(state_code, county_code)
  ) %>%
  select(county_full, county_fips)

life_expectancy_clean <- life_expectancy %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(county != "(blank)", !is.na(census_tract_number)) %>%
  left_join(fips_xwalk, by = c("county" = "county_full")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(county_fips)) %>%   # drops non-NY counties, which won't match the NY-only crosswalk
  mutate(
    tract_clean = str_remove(census_tract_number, "\\.") %>% str_pad(6, pad = "0"),
    GEOID = paste0(county_fips, tract_clean)
  )

life_expectancy_county_nys <- life_expectancy_clean %>%
  left_join(tract_pop, by = "GEOID") %>%
  group_by(county_fips, state, county) %>%
  summarise(
    life_exp_weighted = weighted.mean(life_expectancy, w = tract_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tracts = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(GEOID = county_fips)
```

## 6. Correctional Employment (QCEW, NAICS 92214)

Due to disclosure suppression affecting most county-level records (few
employers per county for this industry code), employment is coded as a
three-category variable (`reported` / `suppressed` / `none`) rather than a
purely continuous measure. QCEW's `agglvl_code` for "county-level, by
ownership" changed from 77 to 78 in the 2024 release; a year-to-code lookup
handles this without hardcoding a single value across all years.

```{r}
years_needed <- c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

agglvl_lookup <- c(
  "2019" = 77, "2020" = 77, "2021" = 77,
  "2022" = 77, "2023" = 77, "2024" = 78
)

occupation_nys_19_24 <- map_dfr(years_needed, function(yr) {
  file_path <- paste0("data/correctional_employment_", yr, ".csv")
  occ_raw <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  target_code <- agglvl_lookup[[as.character(yr)]]

  occ_raw %>%
    filter(agglvl_code == target_code, substr(area_fips, 1, 2) == "36") %>%
    group_by(area_fips) %>%
    summarise(
      correctional_emplvl = sum(annual_avg_emplvl, na.rm = TRUE),
      any_suppressed      = any(disclosure_code == "N"),
      any_reported        = any(is.na(disclosure_code) & annual_avg_emplvl > 0),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      corr_employ_cat = case_when(
        any_reported   ~ "reported",
        any_suppressed ~ "suppressed",
        TRUE           ~ "none"
      ),
      year = yr
    ) %>%
    rename(GEOID = area_fips)
})
```

---

## 7. Domestic Violence (NYS DCJS, 2019–2024)

Raw files vary in extension (`.xls` for 2019–2023, `.xlsx` for 2024). Each
year's sheet has the county name in column 1 filled only on the first row of
each county's block (`fill()` propagates it down), and the last several rows
are source citations / footnotes rather than data, which are filtered out
explicitly by pattern rather than a hardcoded row count (a fixed `slice()` cut
proved fragile across years with differing footer lengths).

```{r}
nys_violence_all <- map_dfr(years_needed, function(yr) {
  ext <- if (yr == 2024) "xlsx" else "xls"
  file_path <- paste0("data/nys_violence_", yr, ".", ext)
  raw <- read_excel(file_path)

  raw %>%
    rename(
      county = 1,
      offense_type = 2,
      female_intimate_partner = 3,
      male_intimate_partner = 4,
      total_intimate_partner = 5,
      other_family_victim = 6,
      total_all_victims = 7
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(female_intimate_partner:total_all_victims), as.numeric)) %>%
    fill(county) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(female_intimate_partner, male_intimate_partner, other_family_victim),
      names_to = "victim_type",
      values_to = "count"
    ) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(county),
      !grepl("DOMESTIC VIOLENCE VICTIMS REPORTED IN", county),
      county != "NON-NEW YORK CITY COUNTIES"
    ) %>%
    mutate(year = yr)
})

nys_violence_wide <- nys_violence_all %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(county, year),
    names_from = c(offense_type, victim_type),
    values_from = count,
    names_glue = "{offense_type}_{victim_type}"
  )
```

Remaining footer rows (source citations, summary totals) that don't correspond
to real counties are dropped, and a naming inconsistency ("St Lawrence" vs.
ACS's "St. Lawrence") is corrected so the county name will match cleanly later.

```{r}
nys_violence_wide <- nys_violence_wide %>%
  mutate(county = if_else(county == "St Lawrence", "St. Lawrence", county)) %>%
  filter(
    !grepl("^Source:", county),
    !grepl("^Total is sum", county),
    county != "Non-New York City Total"
  )
```

## 8. Deaths in Custody (DOCCS)

This file records deaths at the *facility* level, using short operational
names (e.g. "ATTICA") rather than the full official names in `prisons_icpsr`
(e.g. "ATTICA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY"). A manually-verified crosswalk maps each
short name to its full facility name, resolving ambiguous cases (e.g. multiple
"ADIRONDACK"- or "AUBURN"-prefixed facilities) to the correct adult
correctional facility rather than an annex, residential center, or unrelated
facility with a similar name. This crosswalk is reused for the suicides and
staffing files below, since both use the same short-name convention.

```{r}
deaths_in_custody_nys <- read_csv("data/deaths_in_custody_nys.csv")

deaths_clean <- deaths_in_custody_nys %>%
  mutate(
    death_year = year(ymd(DEATH_DATE)),
    facility_name_clean = trimws(toupper(FACILITY_NAME))
  ) %>%
  filter(death_year >= 2019, death_year <= 2024)

facility_crosswalk <- c(
  "GREEN HAVEN" = "GREEN HAVEN CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "MOHAWK" = "MOHAWK CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "AUBURN" = "AUBURN CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",                    # not Residential Center
  "GREAT MEADOW" = "GREAT MEADOW CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "WENDE" = "WENDE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "SING SING" = "SING SING CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "ATTICA" = "ATTICA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "COXSACKIE" = "COXSACKIE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "FISHKILL" = "FISHKILL CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "GREENE" = "GREENE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "RIVERVIEW" = "RIVERVIEW CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "SHAWANGUNK" = "SHAWANGUNK CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "CLINTON" = "CLINTON CORRECTIONAL FACILITY - MAIN",           # ANNEX also exists, same county
  "BEDFORD HILLS" = "BEDFORD HILLS CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "ELMIRA" = "ELMIRA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "MID-STATE" = "MID-STATE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "GROVELAND" = "GROVELAND CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",              # not GROVELAND ANNEX
  "FIVE POINTS" = "FIVE POINTS CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "WOODBOURNE" = "WOODBOURNE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "QUEENSBORO" = "QUEENSBORO CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "ULSTER" = "ULSTER CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "GOWANDA" = "GOWANDA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "WASHINGTON" = "WASHINGTON CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "CAPE VINCENT" = "CAPE VINCENT CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "BARE HILL" = "BARE HILL CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "CAYUGA" = "CAYUGA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "OTISVILLE" = "OTISVILLE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",              # not federal FCI Otisville
  "EASTERN" = "EASTERN NY CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "MARCY" = "MARCY CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "LAKEVIEW" = "LAKEVIEW SHOCK INCARCERATION CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",  # ANNEX also exists, same county
  "ROCHESTER" = "ROCHESTER CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "SULLIVAN" = "SULLIVAN CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "ALBION" = "ALBION CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "DOWNSTATE" = "DOWNSTATE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "FRANKLIN" = "FRANKLIN CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "ALTONA" = "ALTONA CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "GOUVERNEUR" = "GOUVERNEUR CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "COLLINS" = "COLLINS CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "ADIRONDACK" = "ADIRONDACK CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",             # not Residential Center or Wilderness Challenge
  "SOUTHPORT" = "SOUTHPORT CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "WYOMING" = "WYOMING CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "UPSTATE" = "UPSTATE CORRECTIONAL FACILITY",
  "HUDSON" = "HUDSON CORRECTIONAL FACILITY / WORK RELEASE",
  "WALLKILL" = "WALLKILL CORRECTIONAL FACILITY"
)

deaths_matched <- deaths_clean %>%
  mutate(matched_name = facility_crosswalk[facility_name_clean]) %>%
  left_join(ny_facility_lookup_full, by = c("matched_name" = "name_clean"))

# sum(is.na(deaths_matched$COUNTYFIPS)) should be 0 -- confirms every facility name matched

deaths_by_county_year <- deaths_matched %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS, COUNTY, death_year) %>%
  summarise(n_deaths = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS, county_name = COUNTY, year = death_year)
```

## 9. In-Custody Suicides & Staffing Levels (DOCCS)

Both files use the same short facility-naming convention as the deaths file,
so the same `facility_crosswalk` applies directly. Staffing is restricted to
the `TOTAL` category (rather than the security/health/program sub-breakdowns)
for a single overall staffing measure per facility-year.

```{r}
staffing_levels_nys <- read_csv("data/staffing_levels_nys.csv")
suicides_nys <- read_csv("data/suicides_nys.csv")

suicides_matched <- suicides_nys %>%
  mutate(facility_name_clean = trimws(toupper(FACILITY_NAME))) %>%
  mutate(matched_name = facility_crosswalk[facility_name_clean]) %>%
  left_join(ny_facility_lookup_full, by = c("matched_name" = "name_clean")) %>%
  filter(SUICIDE_YEAR >= 2019, SUICIDE_YEAR <= 2024)

suicides_by_county_year <- suicides_matched %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS, COUNTY, SUICIDE_YEAR) %>%
  summarise(n_suicides = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS, county_name = COUNTY, year = SUICIDE_YEAR)

staffing_matched <- staffing_levels_nys %>%
  mutate(
    facility_name_clean = trimws(toupper(FACILITY_NAME)),
    report_year = year(ymd(REPORT_DATE))
  ) %>%
  mutate(matched_name = facility_crosswalk[facility_name_clean]) %>%
  left_join(ny_facility_lookup_full, by = c("matched_name" = "name_clean")) %>%
  filter(report_year >= 2019, report_year <= 2024, STAFFING_CATEGORY == "TOTAL")

staffing_by_county_year <- staffing_matched %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS, COUNTY, report_year) %>%
  summarise(
    budgeted_fill = sum(BUDGETED_FILL_LEVEL, na.rm = TRUE),
    actual_fill   = sum(ACTUAL_FILL_LEVEL, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS, county_name = COUNTY, year = report_year)
```

## 11. Build the Master Panel

Multi-year sources join on `GEOID` + `year`; static (single-snapshot) sources
join on `GEOID` alone and repeat across all years for that county.

```{r}
prisons_static <- prisons_by_county_nys %>% rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS)
rural_static <- rural_2023_nys %>% rename(GEOID = FIPS)
life_exp_static <- life_expectancy_county_nys

master_nys <- census_data_nys %>%
  left_join(injury_overdose_violence_nys, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(occupation_nys_19_24, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(deaths_by_county_year, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(suicides_by_county_year, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(staffing_by_county_year, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(prisons_static, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(rural_static, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(life_exp_static, by = "GEOID")

#nrow(master_nys) #should be 310 (62 NY counties x 5 years)
```

### Clean county name

Several sources carry their own county-name column, in inconsistent formats
(e.g. "Chautauqua County, New York" vs. "CHAUTAUQUA"). Rather than coalescing
across the messy joined versions, a single clean name is built from ACS (the
most complete, consistently-formatted source) and re-attached.

```{r}
county_name_lookup <- census_data_nys %>%
  distinct(GEOID, NAME) %>%
  mutate(county_name_clean = str_remove(NAME, " County, New York")) %>%
  select(GEOID, county_name_clean)

master_nys <- master_nys %>%
  select(-any_of(c("county_name", "county_name.x", "county_name.y", "NAME", "NAME.x", "NAME.y"))) %>%
  left_join(county_name_lookup, by = "GEOID") %>%
  rename(county_name = county_name_clean)

# master_nys %>% distinct(GEOID, county_name) %>% count(GEOID) %>% filter(n > 1)  # should be empty
```

### Structural zeros

Counties with no prison genuinely have zero prison-related deaths, suicides,
staffing, and correctional employment — these `NA`s (from the left joins,
where no matching facility-level record existed) are structural zeros, not
missing data, and are recoded accordingly.

```{r}
master_nys <- master_nys %>%
  mutate(
    n_deaths = replace_na(n_deaths, 0),
    n_suicides = replace_na(n_suicides, 0),
    budgeted_fill = replace_na(budgeted_fill, 0),
    actual_fill = replace_na(actual_fill, 0),
    correctional_emplvl = replace_na(correctional_emplvl, 0),
    corr_employ_cat = replace_na(corr_employ_cat, "none"),
    num_prisons = replace_na(num_prisons, 0),
    num_open = replace_na(num_open, 0),
    num_closed = replace_na(num_closed, 0),
    capacity_total = replace_na(capacity_total, 0),
    pop_total = replace_na(pop_total, 0)
  )
```

### Join domestic violence data

`nys_violence_wide` is keyed by county name string rather than `GEOID`, so it
joins via `county_name_lookup` rather than directly.

```{r}
nys_violence_wide_joined <- nys_violence_wide %>%
  left_join(county_name_lookup, by = c("county" = "county_name_clean")) %>%
  rename(county_name = county)

# sum(is.na(nys_violence_wide_joined$GEOID)) should be 0

master_nys <- master_nys %>%
  left_join(
    nys_violence_wide_joined %>% select(-county_name),
    by = c("GEOID", "year")
  ) %>%
  select(-starts_with("NA_"))   # drops pivot artifacts from originally-NA offense_type rows

# nrow(master_nys) should still be 310
```

## 12. Construct Rate Variables

Raw counts aren't comparable across counties of different population sizes.
Custody-related and domestic violence outcomes are standardized per 100,000
county population; compositional variables are expressed as proportions.

```{r}
master_nys <- master_nys %>%
  mutate(
    prison_present = as.integer(num_open > 0),

    # Custody-related outcomes, per 100k county population
    deaths_in_custody_rate   = n_deaths / tot_pop * 100000,
    suicides_in_custody_rate = n_suicides / tot_pop * 100000,

    # Domestic violence, per 100k population
    dv_total_rate = (Total_female_intimate_partner + Total_male_intimate_partner + Total_other_family_victim) / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_female_rate = (`Agg Assault_female_intimate_partner` + `Simple Assault_female_intimate_partner` +
                       `Sex Offense_female_intimate_partner` + `Violate Protection Order_female_intimate_partner`) / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_male_rate   = (`Agg Assault_male_intimate_partner` + `Simple Assault_male_intimate_partner` +
                       `Sex Offense_male_intimate_partner` + `Violate Protection Order_male_intimate_partner`) / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_agg_assault_rate = (`Agg Assault_female_intimate_partner` + `Agg Assault_male_intimate_partner` + `Agg Assault_other_family_victim`) / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_sex_offense_rate = (`Sex Offense_female_intimate_partner` + `Sex Offense_male_intimate_partner` + `Sex Offense_other_family_victim`) / tot_pop * 100000,

    # Correctional employment, per 100k population
    correctional_emplvl_rate = correctional_emplvl / tot_pop * 100000,

    # Prison staffing gap: positive = understaffed relative to budget
    staffing_gap_pct = (budgeted_fill - actual_fill) / budgeted_fill,

    # Economic / demographic percentages
    poverty_rate      = pop_poverty / pop_poverty_universe,
    unemp_rate        = unemployed / labor_force*100,
    pct_white         = white / tot_pop,
    pct_black         = black / tot_pop,
    pct_asian         = asian / tot_pop,
    pct_hispanic      = hispanic / tot_pop,
    homeown_rate      = hu_ownocc / tot_hu,
    pct_bachelors_plus = edu_bachelors_plus / edu_total,
    pct_hs_or_less     = edu_hs_or_less / edu_total,
    divorce_rate       = divorced / tot_pop,
    rent_burdened_30plus_rate = (rent_burden_30_35 + rent_burden_35_40 + rent_burden_40_50 + rent_burden_50plus) / rent_total,
    single_parent_rate = (single_dad_children + single_mom_children) / tot_hu
  )
```

```{r}
# Sanity check: no negative rates should remain (would indicate an unhandled sentinel value)
range(master_nys$suicide_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
range(master_nys$homicide_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
range(master_nys$overdose_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## Analysis

Exploratory comparison of county-year outcomes by whether the county has an
open prison. **Caveat:** this is a county-*year* panel (each county appears up
to 5 times), so a plain two-sample t-test treats repeated observations from
the same county as independent, which they are not — p-values here should be
read as a first look, not a final result. A clustered-SE regression (e.g. via
`fixest::feols(..., cluster = ~GEOID)`) is the more defensible version for
anything reported formally.

```{r}
table(master_nys$prison_present)
```

```{r}
vars_to_test <- c(
  dv_total_rate = "DV Rate (Total)",
  dv_female_rate = "DV Rate (Female victims)",
  dv_male_rate = "DV Rate (Male victims)",
  dv_agg_assault_rate = "DV Rate (Agg. Assault)",
  dv_sex_offense_rate = "DV Rate (Sex Offense)",
  suicide_rate = "Suicide Rate (community)",
  overdose_rate = "Overdose Rate",
  homicide_rate = "Homicide Rate",
  life_exp_weighted = "Life Expectancy",
  divorce_rate = "Divorce Rate",
  medhhinc = "Median HH Income",
  poverty_rate = "Poverty Rate",
  unemp_rate = "Unemployment Rate",
  homeown_rate = "Homeownership Rate",
  pct_bachelors_plus = "% Bachelor's+",
  single_parent_rate = "Single-Parent Rate"
)

run_ttest_table <- function(data, title, subtitle) {
  results <- lapply(names(vars_to_test), function(v) {
    d <- data %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
    t_result <- t.test(d[[v]] ~ d$prison_present)
    tibble(
      variable = vars_to_test[[v]],
      mean_no_prison = t_result$estimate[1],
      mean_prison = t_result$estimate[2],
      difference = t_result$estimate[2] - t_result$estimate[1],
      p_value = t_result$p.value
    )
  }) %>% bind_rows()

  results %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      variable = "Variable", mean_no_prison = "No Prison",
      mean_prison = "Prison Present", difference = "Difference", p_value = "p-value"
    ) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(mean_no_prison, mean_prison, difference), decimals = 3) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
    tab_header(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) %>%
    tab_style(style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"), locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05))
}

run_ttest_table(
  master_nys,
  "NY County Outcomes by Prison Presence",
  "Two-sample t-tests, county-year observations, 2019-2024"
)
```

### Check for a population/urbanicity confound

```{r}
master_nys %>%
  group_by(prison_present) %>%
  summarise(mean_rucc = mean(RUCC_2023, na.rm = TRUE), mean_pop = mean(tot_pop, na.rm = TRUE))
```

RUCC is similar across groups, but prison-present counties average roughly 4x
the population of no-prison counties — worth controlling for population (and
likely excluding NYC, given its outsized influence on the "no prison" group)
before treating any result above as more than exploratory.

### Repeat excluding NYC

```{r}
nyc_geoids <- c("36005", "36047", "36061", "36081", "36085")  # Bronx, Kings, New York, Queens, Richmond

master_nys_no_nyc <- master_nys %>% filter(!GEOID %in% nyc_geoids)

run_ttest_table(
  master_nys_no_nyc,
  "NY County Outcomes by Prison Presence (Excluding NYC)",
  "Two-sample t-tests, county-year observations, 2019-2024"
)
```
